claims.text: Uniformly dispersed, thermally stable coherent nanoprecipitates enhance high-temperature plastic strain in tungsten-based refractory high-entropy alloys.
Uniformly dispersed, thermally stable coherent nanoprecipitates improve toughness in tungsten-based refractory high-entropy alloys.
Coherent nanoprecipitates promote smooth dislocation glide.
Coherent nanoprecipitates mitigate local stress concentrations.
Mitigation of local stress concentrations delays crack nucleation under fusion plasma-facing conditions.
The initial tungsten-based refractory high-entropy alloy has a BCC matrix.
The initial alloy lacks controlled nanoprecipitate formation.
Optimized spark plasma sintering can produce a uniform dispersion of nanoscale coherent precipitates in the alloy.
Coherent precipitate–BCC matrix interfaces facilitate smooth dislocation transmission.
Smooth dislocation transmission mitigates elevated-temperature strain localization.
SCCP-processed material will exhibit greater plastic strain than the baseline at approximately 800 °C.
SCCP-processed material will exhibit greater toughness than the baseline at approximately 800 °C.
SCCP processing will delay crack initiation relative to the baseline.
The proposed mechanism applies near 800 °C only while the nanoprecipitates remain coherent during prolonged exposure.
Coarsening, dissolution, or loss of precipitate coherence may diminish the proposed strengthening and toughening mechanism.

contradictions.description: The boundary limits the hypothesis to conditions in which precipitates remain coherent, but the falsification rule treats loss of coherence as falsification. Loss of coherence would instead place the experiment outside the stated validity domain and would show failure to realize or retain the mediator, not necessarily refute the conditional mechanism.
